title: Interacting pair failures with a clean edge are #P-hard
claim: p >= 5, r | p - 1, n graded of class at most 4 with a grading-preserving C_r action, d | r, m = m_d the ideal of nonzero characters, k in {0, gamma_4(m)} with m/k of class at most 3. A clean edge is a hard pair (alpha, beta) of (m/k)/gamma_3 with slot types alpha (vertex), beta, gamma = alpha + beta such that brackets between layer-1 characters of distinct leaves lie in gamma_3 outside the characters forced by the private duals, the layer-3 brackets of the two private leaves avoid the vertex roots, and k avoids the active characters. If a clean edge exists, counting |Hom(pi_1 S^3_(d/p)(K), G)| is #P-hard. Proof: zero-jump gadget knots (blocks returning exactly to the meridian value, dedicated vertex copies, Brunnian commutator insertions) make the pinned count an edge-local integer partition function on the layer-2 variety; the edge count is maximal on the diagonal and strictly smaller but positive across a pair-failing difference (Brunnian rank lemma); subdivision gives the symmetric matrix F F^T of rank at least two; anchor isolation recovers the total count.
failure_conditions: A cabled commutator braid whose conjugators do not vanish when a bundle is deleted, or a zero-jump block whose end strand differs from its base strand or whose copies differ from the reading strand under some pinned representation.
An algebra listed as having a clean edge that violates a stated condition, or a census count of clean edges other than 50 of 176.
For free class 3 on (1, 1) at d = 5, p = 11: an edge count with F(s, s) < F_max, F(0, D) = F_max for D != 0, or rank F F^T < 2.

An open-algebra breakdown by minimal failing conditions other than the one stated in proof.md (126 algebras; 26 blocked only by (K), 12 only by (V3), 10 only by (B2), 4 without a hard pair modulo gamma_3).
On the single-edge gadget at the diagonal: vertex equations vanishing for the stated (K)-only or (V3)-only example, or not vanishing for the stated (B2)-only example.
foundation_claim_scope: p >= 5, r | p - 1, graded nilpotent Lie algebras of class at most 4 with a grading-preserving C_r action; manifolds S^3_(d/p)(K). Cited: the triple-construction lemmas (COPRIME-PAIRS-20261027-001A), the reductions (COPRIME-PAIRS-20261027-001C), Lemma I, Bulatov-Grohe via Cai-Chen-Lu. Not covered: interacting pair failures without a clean edge (126 of 850 census algebras), class at least 5, non-graded algebras, p = 2, 3. r counts the characters of the action, not Boolean variables. No P versus NP claim.

validation.status: checked: the cabled commutator braid fixes the remaining strands when a bundle is deleted (free group, d = 2..6); zero-jump blocks carry exact base and reading values under random pinned lifts on amphichiral and cable summands; 50 of the 176 interacting census algebras have a clean edge (Theorem 4) and 5 more under the character-0 refinement (Theorem 5), with (V3) including the leaves' determined layer-2 parts; the open algebras by minimal failing sets; for free class 3 on (1,1) at d = 5 the full 121 x 121 edge matrix has F(s,s) = F_max, F(0,D) < F_max for D != 0 and rank F F^T = 121; diagonal vertex equations nonzero for a (K)-only and a (V3)-only algebra, zero for the first Theorem 5 algebra, which also passes the diagonal, deficit and on-variety path tests; frozen experiment COPRIME-PAIRS-20261027-001D-E001 refuted by an off-variety locality rule, successor E002 supported on five algebras with three controls; no human or external review
